source_title: Samsung Galaxy Fit 4 looks close to launch, and its biggest features just leaked
source_excerpt:

A teardown of the Galaxy Fit 4’s companion app has revealed nearly all of its features.
The budget tracker could offer a similar set of health tracking features as the Galaxy Fit 3.
It could come with a slightly taller display, use the same tile-based UI, and support 12 tiles.
Samsung is expected to launch the Galaxy Fit 4 budget fitness tracker sometime this year. We’ve already reported on documentation hinting at the tracker and exclusively shared 360-degree views of the Galaxy Fit 4 a few months ago. Now, a new leak is giving us a detailed look at the upcoming fitness tracker’s features.
SammyGuru ‘s teardown of the Galaxy Fit 4 Manager app has spilled nearly every feature the fitness tracker could offer, and it seems very similar to the Galaxy Fit 3 from 2024.
The teardown revealed daily tracking support for steps, active time, and activity calories. These are low-hanging fruit that one would expect on any fitness tracker worth its salt. The Galaxy Fit 4 could also include stress tracking and send alerts if a user experiences high stress for an extended period.
The fitness tracker could also support heart rate monitoring, along with alerts for high or low heart rate readings. In addition, it could offer support for heart rate zones, which can come in handy while working out.
Other health features revealed by the teardown include sleep tracking, complete with information about sleep stages, a sleep score, and personalized sleep coaching after seven recorded nights. It could also support blood oxygen monitoring, snoring detection, automatic workout tracking, cycle tracking, food and water tracking, and more.
Nearly all of these features were also available on the Galaxy Fit 3, which launched in 2024. Surprisingly, Samsung doesn’t seem to be adding anything new. However, the company could be betting on other upgrades for the Fit 4, such as improved battery life or more accurate tracking.
The outlet also spotted several new banners, animations, and images showcasing how users could interact with the Galaxy Fit 4. Samsung could continue using the tile-based UI, with the teardown hinting at support for adding up to 12 tiles.
The tracker is said to also feature a swipe-based navigation system, the same as the Fit 3. Users will likely be able to swipe to access quick settings, notifications, or apps. Additionally, users will be able to find their phone using their Galaxy Fit 4, according to screenshots spotted in the teardown.
The teardown also revealed watch face assets with a resolution of 258 x 428 pixels. That resolution will likely match the tracker’s screen resolution, implying a slightly taller display than the Galaxy Fit 3.
Samsung has yet to announce a release date for the Galaxy Fit 4, or even confirm that the tracker is coming this year. However, with the tracker getting FCC and BIS certifications, Samsung will likely launch it sooner rather than later.
